title: What is a stored procedure and how does it differ from a function?
description: Understand stored procedures vs functions in SQL Server.

data.text: **Question:** What is a stored procedure and how does it differ from a function?

A stored procedure is a precompiled set of SQL statements that can perform operations. Unlike functions, stored procedures can modify data, have side effects, and use transactions. Functions must return a value and cannot modify database state.

**Stored Procedure:**
- Can perform DML operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)
- Can have side effects
- Can use transactions
- Can return multiple result sets
- Can call other stored procedures
- Executed using EXEC or EXECUTE

**Function:**
- Must return a value
- Cannot modify database state
- Cannot use transactions
- Can only return one result set
- Can be used in SQL queries
- Executed using SELECT or in queries

data.title: Stored Procedure vs Function
data.code:
-- Stored Procedure
CREATE PROCEDURE GetEmployeeOrders
    @EmployeeId INT
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE EmployeeId = @EmployeeId;
    UPDATE Employees SET LastAccess = GETDATE() WHERE Id = @EmployeeId;
END

-- Function
CREATE FUNCTION GetEmployeeName(@Id INT)
RETURNS NVARCHAR(100)
AS
BEGIN
    RETURN (SELECT Name FROM Employees WHERE Id = @Id);
END
-- Can be used in SELECT
SELECT dbo.GetEmployeeName(1);

data.text: Interviewers want to assess understanding of when to use stored procedures vs functions and their practical differences.

items: When should you use a stored procedure?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Functions can be used in queries
data.takeaway: Use stored procedures for complex operations and functions for computations within queries.
